kinds.d: Fossil ammonoid shell, whole, split, polished or on matrix, including unworked stones kept for a religious tradition.

x.d: Involute, high-whorled Albian ammonite from Madagascar, Europe and the Transcaspian region, often sold split and polished.
Widespread Lower Jurassic ammonite (about 180 million years old) with strong forward-leaning ribs; an index fossil.
x.dt: about 65 mm across · about 70 species · England, Germany · mass-mortality slabs

x.d: Lower Jurassic ammonite from Lyme Regis, Dorset, collected from the obtusum zone of the Upper Sinemurian.
Late Cretaceous ammonite from Asia, Europe and the Americas, source of most gem ammolite.

v.d: Species also found in the Pierre Shale of Montana and South Dakota
Species of the Bearpaw Formation, Alberta

x.d: Almost straight heteromorph ammonite of the Late Cretaceous, named by Lamarck in 1799; common in rock shops.
Bizarrely shaped heteromorph ammonite from about 76 million years ago whose shell spirals upwards into a hooked tip.
Ammonite stone collected from the Kali Gandaki river in Nepal and India and worshipped in Hinduism as a form of Vishnu.

kinds.d: Gem-quality iridescent ammonite shell material, rough or cut.

x.d: Iridescent aragonite shell of Placenticeras ammonites from the Bearpaw Formation, mined mostly along the St. Mary River in southern Alberta.

v.d: Official gemstone status granted and commercial mining began

x.dt: red and green most common · blue and purple rarer · grades AAA to A− (not standardised)

x.d: Composite stones: thin ammolite on a dark backing (doublet) with a transparent convex cap (triplet).
x.dt: backing of matrix, onyx or glass · cap of synthetic spinel, corundum, quartz or glass

kinds.d: Fossil coiled nautiloid shell, whole, split or polished. Straight-shelled nautiloids such as Orthoceras are listed here too; belemnites are a different group.

x.d: Straight-shelled nautiloid; strictly Orthoceras regulare of the Middle Ordovician limestones of Sweden and the Baltic, though the name was long used for many orthocones.
x.dt: simple suture line · often confused with Baculites in shops

x.d: Extinct genus of the nautilid family Nautilidae, described by Hyatt in 1884; type species Cenoceras intermedium.

kinds.d: Fossil belemnite guard, the solid calcite tip of an extinct squid-like cephalopod.

x.d: Late Cretaceous belemnite of Europe and North America; the state fossil of Delaware since 1996.
Guards of genera such as Cylindroteuthis and Hibolithes, found from the Jurassic into the Early Cretaceous.

v.d: Early Jurassic to Early Cretaceous; Asia, Europe, North America, New Zealand
Middle Jurassic to Early Cretaceous; many continents

x.dt: called thunderbolts in folklore · polished sections

brands.d: Calgary-based miner and the largest commercial producer of gem ammolite, supplying over 90% of it.

notes: Orthoceras alias moved from Belemnite to Fossil nautiloid. Moroccan Orthoceras and pyritised Lyme Regis ammonites not covered: no retrieved page confirmed them. Ammonite kept as one kind with Shaligram as the religious-stone archetype.
